A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, figures, and complete appendices. v3 Appendices A/B/C correspond to v4 Appendices C/A/B, allowing reliable comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic-network experiments, image and text classification analyses, and CIFAR-100-to-CIFAR-10 transfer experiments, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the SST-5 and ImageNet analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The deep linear network formulation, MSE objective, gradient-descent procedure, initialization, and feature-compression/discrimination framework are retained. No proposed algorithm or methodological component is added or changed.

E1.justification: Both versions cover nearly orthogonal synthetic data, CIFAR-10, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-100-to-CIFAR-10 transfer, SST-5, and ImageNet. Moving the supplementary experiments from Appendix C to B does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same MLP-versus-hybrid comparisons and network-depth/projection-head configurations. No comparison method is added or removed; revised layer counts concern reported settings.

E3.justification: Section 5.1.1 revises the reported configuration from seven layers and 200 epochs to eight layers, explicitly including the classifier, and 400 epochs. Section 5.2.2 replaces the stated nine-layer networks with a six-layer DLN and ten-layer MLP, matching the existing plots. These reporting revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The depth, width, initialization, training-versus-initialization, projection-head, and low-rankness analyses retain the same questions and evidence. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is introduced or removed.

E5.justification: v4 Figure 7 explicitly identifies its existing error bars as standard deviations. Corresponding v3 Figure 6 reports means from ten random seeds without defining the bars. Run counts and the other uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All 17 matched figures retain identical plotted content, including the appendix results, and the qualitative findings remain unchanged. Revised architecture and training-budget descriptions do not introduce altered numerical outcomes.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, main bounds, proposition, auxiliary lemmas, and proofs are mathematically unchanged. Theorem 1 becomes Theorem 4, while the proof and auxiliary appendices are reordered; notation and equation-display changes do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about geometric within-class compression, linear between-class discrimination, relevance to nonlinear networks, and implications for transfer learning.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 adds an explanation that between-class normalization avoids spuriously small compression scores near total feature collapse. Section 3.2 qualifies broader validity of the weight assumptions as something that empirically 'seems to hold,' replacing v3's more definite assertion.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly documents plotting ranges for compression and discrimination and clarifies inclusion of the final classifier in the experimental layer count. The stated training budget is revised, while hardware and code-access information remain the same.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Achour et al. (2024), Chen et al. (2025), and Yaras et al. (2024), while removing Section 4's dedicated NTK comparison and several other citations. The central positioning relative to neural collapse and hierarchical feature learning remains intact.

P1.justification: Extensive copyediting and sentence rewriting span the abstract and main text. The contents page and introductory subsection heading are removed, the appendices are reordered, and the bibliography moves after them, producing a broad editorial reorganization.

P2.justification: v4 redesigns the first page, introduces running headers and different caption typography, reformats equations, and reflows figures throughout. v3 Figure 12 moves into the introduction as v4 Figure 4, and the initialization figures share a page. The underlying plot panels are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves clarity through copyediting, explicit standard-deviation labeling, the normalization explanation, and correction of Section 5.2.2's layer counts to match its plots. The theory and empirical evidence remain unchanged. Newly erroneous appendix theorem references and inconsistent SST-5 layer-count descriptions limit these gains, but the overall improvement in explanation and reporting is modestly positive.
